text:
maya: heads up — nightly evals flagged a regression on the answer-quality metric for model-redwood-v2-quant after last night's infra roll.
liam: saw that alert. which testset? shortdev or our large benchmark suite?
sophia: large-bench. the delta is ~3.8% on exact-match over the comp-sens benchmark, started at ~23:00 UTC.
maya: included some logs in the CI run: https://ci.redwood/internal/runs/98765 — looks correlated with commit 7f3a2d1 (runtime: batching change)
alex: assigning to me to triage. first step: replicate locally with the same quantized build.
liam: quick attempt: repro doesn't show on cpu-only, but on gpus with q8-runtime I can reproduce ~2.9% dip.
sophia: interesting — we recently landed a kernel selector tweak that prefers fused attention kernels when seq_len<256. commit 7f3a2d1 touches that.
maya: can you bisect to isolate the exact commit?
alex: running git bisect now across the release branch. running eval-runner with same seed + dataset.
ci-bot: Test run queued: eval-runner job 17902 on gpu-pool-2. Params: model=model-redwood-v2-quant, batch=8, seed=42.
liam: while bisect runs, can we sanity-check metric calc? there were a few changes to the exact-match scoring earlier this month.
sophia: looked at scorer change — only whitespace normalization tweak, unrelated.
alex: bisect got narrowed: bad commit introduced at 7f3a2d1 -> 7f3f9b8. repro consistent across two different GPU types.
maya: so looks like runtime change is likely. any quick mitigations? rollback of the kernel selector tweak or pin kernel to previous behavior?
liam: we can add a temporary flag to force the old selector per model, but that requires a hotfix deploy to dedicated.
sophia: another thing — the quantization profile updated on the model side last week (q8->q4 hybrid). Could interactions cause regression? alex: I ran both q8-only and hybrid; regression only when runtime picks fused kernels + q4 hybrid.
alex: here's the local repro command I used:
```
./eval-runner --model model-redwood-v2-quant --quant-profile hybrid-q4 --batch-size 8 --seed 42 --dataset comp-sens
```
logs show dropout in exact-match from 0.372 -> 0.338 across runs.
maya: would be ideal to have a minimal reproducer to attach to the runtime PR for review.
liam: I created a tiny harness that runs 200 examples to show the delta. pushing branch `ml/mini-repro-fused-kernel` now.
ci-bot: Build passed for ml/mini-repro-fused-kernel. Artifacts: s3://artifacts/mini-repro/17902
sophia: alex — can you attach the bisect output and the harness results to the runtime PR? Also request a revert if the change is high-risk.
alex: done. PR #4123 updated with bisect info and mini-repro link.
maya: decision time — do we rollback immediately or ship a targeted fix? impact is on production quality for some models, but not all.
liam: my vote is rollback the kernel selector tweak for the release branch, then iterate on a fix in dev. we don't want subtle regressions creeping into Dedicated customers.
sophia: agreed. I'll open the revert PR for the release branch. tagging infra oncall.
alex: revert PR #4128 created — deploy job queued.
ci-bot: Deploy to release branch started: deploy/17903. Canary on 5% traffic.
liam: monitoring canary now. metrics dashboard link: https://observability.redwood/evals/runs/17903
maya: canary shows metric back to baseline within noise — exact-match 0.371 -> 0.374 after revert.
sophia: rolling out full revert. will keep the bisect notes and mini-repro attached for the follow-up investigation.
alex: follow-up items: (1) add regression unit to CI that exercises fused vs unfused kernels for quantized flows, (2) add metric gating for exact-match delta > 2% on release, (3) more test coverage in runner.
maya: thanks everyone. filing incident ticket and change note for release managers.
liam: nice triage turnaround. :thumbsup:
sophia: leaving a postmortem checklist in #postmortems in case we need it.
maya: closing thread once deploys finish. will ping if anything else pops up.
